design.md's Protected-File Statement, point 5 (lines 301-303, added by commit cf631ea7, the sole change this round re-binds) cites its own authority as an unelaborated human ruling on the T-001 cross-model panel's cross-target-atomicity finding, and no other source. This is a change to the protected-file human-copy / feature-scoped anchored-runner boundary that security-spec.md names as boundary B5 (security-spec.md:31, 50-51, 63, 74). investigation.md's own Amendment Re-Review Context section (investigation.md:696 onward) is this package's established, and so far exhaustively used, mechanism for recording every other human ruling and document amendment in this same package with full commit hashes, per-document SHA-256 fingerprints as of each amendment commit, and verbatim dated approval quotations (e.g. investigation.md:761-766's two quoted approvals; the extension at investigation.md:804-1035+ tracking commits through 23fe659f, 2026-08-25, in the same rigorous form). That section contains no entry, no commit hash, and no verbatim quotation for commit cf631ea7 (the commit that authored this exact point) or for any cross-target-atomicity finding by any panel. Concrete failure mode: nothing in the manifest-pinned artifact set lets a reviewer or later auditor verify that the cited ruling occurred, who issued it, or what its scope was, for a change to a security-relevant boundary rather than a cosmetic edit. Per reviewer-calibration.md's own Amendment Re-Review Context section, the amendment-disclosure suppression it grants only applies when the investigation.md entry covers the whole completion chain, listing every commit an amendment grew across; since this package's own most recent amendment, and the one most consequential to this round, is absent from that chain, the suppression does not extend to it, and the uncited authority claim stands as an ordinary finding. This is not a precheck-owned concern (precheck checks hash/status only, not investigation.md narrative completeness). Rated Major rather than Critical because point 5's own technical content is otherwise internally consistent with the rest of the Protected-File Statement and does not itself misstate a fact; only its own claimed authorization is unverifiable from the review manifest. This package's own acceptance-tests.md (lines 136-142) records a comparable provenance mismatch having been rated Critical by a prior reviewer, which is why this is flagged rather than passed over. Secondary, non-blocking observation on the same point: point 5's own second paragraph (lines 318-329) states it corrects the scope of point 4, which reads as though the only post-copy verification is the batch-wide pass; a real and fair self-correction, but it corrects point 4 by adding a forward disclaimer in point 5 rather than editing point 4's own text; a reader who stops at point 4 alone would still form the incomplete picture point 5 describes. This is a structural readability note, not a contradiction (point 5 explicitly reconciles it), and does not independently affect the verdict.

design.md's Test Strategy item 17 (lines 955-964) is the sole Test Strategy item mapped to AC-031 (requirements.md:830) and its acceptance-tests.md row (acceptance-tests.md:54), the runner-conformance acceptance criterion for the feature-scoped anchored human-copy runner. Item 17's own text, and both of those rows' own text, each name only the exact-set / per-target-hash / post-copy-verification properties (points 1-4 of the Protected-File Statement's runner contract) as what must be confirmed or, once authored, rejected/enumerated by a fixture. None of the three citations mentions the fifth point's own new properties: per-target atomic publish (temp file, fsync, digest-check, atomic rename), the explicit no-rollback acknowledgment, the live-state reporting obligation on failure (enumerating which targets are installed, which failed, and which were never attempted), or the recovery-by-rerun/idempotent-reapply property (design.md:301-329, added by commit cf631ea7, this round's sole design.md change). A search of requirements.md and of design.md's own Test Strategy section for wording naming rollback, installed-target enumeration, not-attempted enumeration, or live-state reporting returns no match outside the Protected-File Statement's own point 5 text. Concrete failure mode: a future implementation task can satisfy every currently-traceable acceptance criterion for this runner (exact-set, hash, post-copy) while never building or verifying a fixture for the fifth point's own atomicity/reporting/recovery properties, since no acceptance criterion or Test Strategy item requires one, which is precisely the property a human ruling introduced this point to guarantee gets built and verified, per the point's own text requiring the runner to report live state before it exits on any failure after the copy phase has begun. Not precheck-owned (precheck checks hash/status only, not acceptance-criterion-to-Test-Strategy-item completeness). Major: this is a coverage gap likely to cause failed or incomplete verification of a newly added, human-ruled-in, security-relevant requirement.
